description: Jean Valjean looks for redemption in a France that refuses to forgive him. Hugo mixes love story, historical chronicle and a plea for the outcast.

hero.hook: A stolen loaf of bread, nineteen years at hard labor, then a whole life spent proving that a man can become a man again.

blocks.text: Published in **1862**, **Les Misérables** is one of the most widely read novels in the world. **Victor Hugo**, poet and campaigning novelist, tells the story of **19th-century** France through **Jean Valjean**, an ex-convict hunted by **[[Inspector Javert]]**. Javert is an incorruptible policeman. He is the law without mercy.

The book mixes detective plot, love story, historical chronicle and social protest. Hugo wanted a “world-book,” a novel that takes in a whole era. He hoped to speak to everyone, across borders. It is also a great text about poverty, grace and the chance to start again.

**Victor Hugo** began the novel as early as **1845**, under the title “Les Misères.” After the **1851** coup of **Napoleon III**, the nephew of Napoleon Bonaparte, Hugo went into exile in the Channel Islands, on Guernsey. He picked up his manuscript again with new fire. Exile fed his anger at injustice.

blocks.caption: Victor Hugo: poet, novelist and voice of the poor

blocks.text: To write the sewer scene, Hugo asked the Paris drainage service for documents and explored the underground galleries himself.

The novel came out in **1862** in Brussels, after seventeen years of work. Hugo packs it with long **[[digressions]]**, pages where the author stops the story to talk about history or philosophy. Some go to **Waterloo**, the 1815 battle that ended the Napoleonic empire, some to convents, some to the **[[sewers of Paris]]**, the underside of the capital and a metaphor for the social unconscious. These pages root the characters in a material reality and turn the book into a treatise of social philosophy.

sections.title: Hugo and a book born in exile

blocks.text: Condemned for stealing a loaf of bread, Valjean spends **19 years** at hard labor in Toulon, ground down by the **[[penal colony and the 19th-century penal system]]**. When he gets out, the **yellow passport** marks him as a former convict. He becomes an outcast. Bishop **Myriel**, known as “Monseigneur Bienvenu,” gives him a second chance: he tells the police that the silver was a gift, when Valjean had just stolen it.

blocks.caption: The prison hulks: the experience that breaks Valjean before his moral rebirth

blocks.text: Jean Valjean, my brother, you belong no longer to evil, but to good.

Under the name **Monsieur Madeleine**, Valjean becomes the philanthropist mayor of an industrial town. For Hugo, charity can defeat social fate. But **Javert**, justice without pity made flesh, never stops hunting him. He cannot imagine that a criminal might turn into a good man.

sections.title: Jean Valjean: from hard labor to grace

blocks.text: **Fantine**, a working woman abandoned by the lover who seduced her, sinks into misery paying for the board of her daughter **Cosette**. The child is left with the **Thénardiers**, greedy innkeepers. Valjean rescues her and becomes her protector. The story moves to Paris, where the uprising of **June 1832**, a republican revolt crushed by the army, gathers the young into the secret society of the **[[ABC]]**. The name is a French pun on *les abaissés*, the downtrodden.

blocks.caption: The barricades of 1832: History walks into the novel

blocks.text: On those barricades dies **Gavroche**, the street child who became a symbol of sacrificed innocence. **Enjolras**, leader of the rebels, stands for idealistic youth. There Valjean saves **Marius**, a young bourgeois in love with Cosette, in an act of total self-denial. He accepts the risk of losing his freedom for the happiness of the girl he treats as his daughter.

**Javert**, whose life Valjean spares during the uprising, cannot hold law and grace together, and he drowns himself in the Seine. Valjean dies at peace, having kept his promise to Myriel. The novel is a pillar of **[[socially engaged literature]]**, writing put at the service of a social or political cause. Hugo attacks the lack of compulsory schooling, the oppression of women and the inhumanity of prisons.

blocks.text: **Les Misérables**, published in **1862**, tells the redemption of **Jean Valjean** between charity and pitiless law. Hugo turns the barricades of **1832** into the symbol of the fight for human dignity.
